name: Rufous-headed Chachalaca
rangeDescription: Western ecuador and far northwestern peru
description: Large chickenlike bird with a long tail. No similar species in limited range; much smaller than Crested Guan and warmer brown than Sickle-winged Guan.

name: Claudia's Leaf Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of western china to eastern tibet; winters to southern china and southeastern asia
description: One of the Blyth’s-type warblers, this species regularly flicks its wings one after the other. Usually forages actively high up in the canopy, clambering along branches.

name: Purple-throated Fruitcrow
rangeDescription: Tropical costa rica to northern bolivia, the guianas, and amazonian brazil
description: Large, mostly black bird found in the canopy of lowland forests. Male has wine-colored throat that can be puffed out expressively, but is often difficult to see in poor light.

name: Pink-headed Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of far southern mexico (chiapas) to guatemala
description: Unmistakable small warbler of highlands in Guatemala and Chiapas. Favors humid conifer forest, pine-oak forest, and adjacent brushy areas; locally fairly common to scarce.

name: Azure Jay
rangeDescription: Southeastern brazil to eastern paraguay and northeastern argentina
description: Large jay found in humid forests, especially Araucaria forests, the seeds of which are the jay’s main food. It has a mostly blue body, which can be ultramarine or cerulean, a black head with a small crest, and a black throat.

name: Magdalena Antbird
rangeDescription: Northern slope of andes of colombia and northwestern venezuela (zulia and mérida)
description: Medium-sized, short-tailed antbird with a bright red eye. Has slate gray head and breast, black throat, brown belly and upperparts, and whitish dotted wings.

name: Scarlet Myzomela
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (cooktown, queensland to eastern victoria)
description: Tiny honeyeater. Adult males have brilliant red coloration on the face and back; it also extends down onto the breast.

name: Orange River White-eye
rangeDescription: Namibia and northern south africa (northern cape, north west, and free state)
description: A small, active, yellow-green warbler-like bird with an obvious white eye-ring. The peach-colored underparts are diagnostic.

name: Gray-headed Bulbul
rangeDescription: Southwestern peninsular india (southern maharashtra and goa to western mysore and kerala)
description: Perpetually surprised-looking bulbul. Predominantly olive-yellow with a gray head, yellow forehead, and silvery rump and tail.

name: Pygmy Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Mountains of new guinea (bird's head peninsula to owen stanley range)
description: A tiny, green lorikeet of foothill and montane forest and edge. Uniform green plumage, light streaking on the chest and slightly elongated pointy tail.

name: Mindanao Serin
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (mount katanglad and mount apo on mindanao)
description: Rare and localized highland finch, restricted to upper montane forest and open scrubby and grassy habitats above the treeline. Generally not very obvious, often foraging quietly in dense growth, but flocks will sometimes betray their presence by flying overhead and giving a chorus of chittering twitter calls.

name: Bali Myna
rangeDescription: Coastal northwestern bali (bali barat national park); extinct in the wild with reintroductions in nusa penida island and (usually unsuccessful) in western bali
description: An eye-catching white starling with black tips to the tail and wings, bare blue facial skin, and long plumes that hang down the nape. Juvenile is shorter-crested than adult, with yellow wash.

name: Mountain Barbet
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern borneo
description: Faded-looking barbet of Borneo’s north-central mountain ranges. Grass-green above and pale green below, with a pale blue head, an off-white throat, and a bright red streak on the back of the head.

name: Tumbes Swallow
rangeDescription: Coastal northwestern peru (tumbes to la libertad) and adjacent southwestern ecuador
description: Desert-loving swallow of northwestern Peru; occasionally (perhaps seasonally) crosses over the border into southwestern Ecuador. The only swallow in its limited range with a white rump.

name: Halmahera Flowerpecker
rangeDescription: Moluccas (morotai, halmahera, kasiruta, bacan, obi, and bisa)
description: A tiny, dumpy, very short-tailed gray songbird. Paler underparts are divided by a whiter central strip.

name: Eleonora's Falcon
rangeDescription: Mediterranean islands and coasts; winters to madagascar
description: Strikingly long-winged and long-tailed elegant falcon with dark underwing coverts. Two plumage morphs: dark morph is uniformly dark while pale morph has white cheeks and a chestnut belly streaked with black.

name: Aberdare Cisticola
rangeDescription: West-central kenya (aberdare mountains)
description: A large and relatively colorful cisticola endemic to Kenya, found locally in montane grassland and moorland. The cap and back of the neck are dull rufous with darker streaking, the back is heavily streaked with black, and there is a rufous panel in the wings.

name: Short-toed Coucal
rangeDescription: Malay peninsula, sumatra, and borneo
description: Burly long-tailed cuckoo. Adult is coal-black with bright rufous wings and back.

name: Black-backed Bittern
rangeDescription: Southwestern and eastern australia and new guinea
description: Tiny secretive heron. Adult male has black back, brown neck, and streaked reddish-brown underparts.

name: Red Phalarope
rangeDescription: Holarctic circumpolar; winters at sea in southern hemisphere
description: The chunkiest and thickest-billed phalarope. Of the three phalaropes, Red is the least likely to be seen inland.
